[IARC.7.10] **CORE-MATH is vendored.** libds compiles the correctly-rounded
functions [LEXP.3.9.2] requires from CORE-MATH's binary64 sources at one pinned
upstream commit, through the same pinned-fetch path as RE2, with the files
unmodified. They are compiled with libds's flags (`-O2 -ffp-contract=off`, and
`-std=gnu11` for the 128-bit integer types) on a toolchain whose
`FLT_EVAL_METHOD` is 0.

A release row whose compiler has no 128-bit integer type must compile the
functions that compute in one from a portable layer instead: copies of those
files at the same upstream commit, in which the 128-bit integer is a class of
two 64-bit words, compiled as C++ with no C++ runtime. The layer is vendored at
a pin of its own, and every change it makes to an upstream file is marked in
that file. The layer must compute what the upstream file computes, bit for bit,
on every input. A release row whose compiler has the type must not use the
layer.

The pin, the layer's pin and the flags are recorded together: a change to any
of them changes the functions, and a release row built with it is admitted again
before it ships ([NDET.1.4], [NDET.1.4.1]).
